title: "Spatial complementarity of FDI: the example of transition countries"
description: >-
  **Post-Communist Economies, 2012.**

  We study the spatial determinants of FDI location — FDI in neighbouring countries and foreign market potential — across a panel of 25 transition countries from 1993 to 2010. Spatial FDI spillovers are positive and economically large; omitting them seriously misspecifies models of FDI location. The complementarity is stronger in disaggregated (bilateral, sector-level) data, with substantial heterogeneity across sectors: spillovers are large and positive in services but non-significant or even negative in manufacturing.
  </details>

Foreign direct investment into one transition country raises, rather than
diverts, FDI into its neighbours — the opposite of the substitution effect
that simple location-competition models predict. We show FDI flows into
this region are spatial complements, most plausibly through shared supply
chains and demonstration effects on investor perceptions of the wider
region.

**Published in:** *Post-Communist Economies*, 24(3), 327–349
